bindings.label: Patient had decreased visual acuity in the right eye (20/80)

Patient had a history of strabismus, hyperopia, and amblyopia in the right eye, multiple odontogenic cysts, and scoliosis; she had been evaluated in Neuropediatrics for macrocephaly, her intellectual capacity was normal, and her mother had undergone surgery for skin cancer and maxillary cysts.
Clinical examination showed visual acuity of 20/80 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye; anterior segment evaluation showed no abnormalities, and intraocular pressure was normal in both eyes.
Fundus examination revealed an elevated white-greyish lesion in the temporal region of the macula with associated vascular distortion, causing significant traction in the macular area.
Macular tractional lesion
Intraocular tumor/hamartoma
Amblyopia/refractive error
Systemic genetic syndrome
OCT shows disorganized retinal layers, hyperreflective mass, and epiretinal membrane
FA shows vascular tortuosity and leakage
Radiologist concluded that objective OCT/FA evidence supports macular tractional lesion as the most credible diagnosis
